item.title: Trump announces 'historic' Gaza deal as Board of Peace agrees on Hamas disarmament
item.description: Donald Trump announced a historic agreement for Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawal. This phased deal will establish a new Palestinian administration in Gaza. The Board of Peace facilitated this monumental step toward lasting peace and security. Mediators Egypt, Qatar, and Türkiye were thanked for their important efforts. Gaza will no longer pose a security threat after this significant progress.

item.title: Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso: "When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to…"
item.description: Pablo Picasso admired children's uninhibited artistic expression and their natural imagination. He believed true mastery combined technical skill with this fearless approach. Older artists often lose this freedom due to fear of judgment and criticism. Picasso's journey shows simplicity achieved through experience is a higher achievement. Rediscovering this childlike curiosity is key to lifelong innovation and creativity.

item.title: Quote by Bertrand Russell: 'There are two motives for reading a book; one, that you enjoy it...'
item.description: Reading serves a dual purpose: it offers personal satisfaction while also catering to the desire for intellectual recognition among peers. This blend of motivations can drive individuals to choose books based on public perception rather than genuine interest. Psychological theories identify this as the contrast between intrinsic and extrinsic motivations. In our digital age, online platforms enhance this performative nature of reading.

item.title: Quote of the day by Leo Tolstoy: 'Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one...'
item.description: According to Leo Tolstoy, true societal change begins with personal evolution. He asserted that individuals must first address their own imperfections. This mindset has significantly shaped leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr. However, in our contemporary society, there is a trend toward prioritizing external grievances over internal growth. To achieve meaningful advancements, it is essential to blend personal honesty with systemic change.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Before they were famous: “The moment you think you’ve made it, you stop growing”: How did Kai Cenat become one of the biggest streamers in the world?
item.description: Kai Cenat’s rise began with comedy videos on Instagram before expanding to YouTube, joining AMP, and later becoming one of Twitch’s biggest stars. His success came through years of consistent work rather than one viral moment. Today, his personality, audience connection, and creative live streams have made him one of the most influential digital creators in the world.

item.title: Scientists transplanted 42 sea sponges into a polluted Spanish marina; 91.7% of one species survived
item.description: In a remarkable experiment, scientists have introduced sea sponges into a polluted marina in Spain to investigate their resilience. The chicken kidney sponge, a particularly robust species, not only survived for an impressive 455 days but also showcased its remarkable ability to reproduce mobile clones. These developments indicate that sponges may play a critical role in ecological restoration, potentially aiding in the detoxification of contaminated coastal areas.

item.title: Boreal forests shade permafrost so effectively that summer thaw stays about one metre shallower
item.description: Thick forest canopies keep northern permafrost cool, safeguarding vast carbon stores. This natural shade prevents soil thawing and the release of greenhouse gases. Researchers discovered this vital cooling service has been largely overlooked in climate models. Losing these forests means losing this crucial protection for underground carbon. Protecting these boreal forests is therefore extremely important for global climate stability.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Montana man impales himself on trekking pole, hikes 10 miles to safety instead of calling helicopter
item.description: A hiking trip to Montana's highest mountain turned into a remarkable survival story after a nurse accidentally impaled himself on a trekking pole but still managed to hike nearly 10 miles to safety instead of waiting for a helicopter rescue. There, surgeons safely removed the trekking pole and treated the wound. Just days later, Cifaldi had already returned to work.

item.title: China spent $13.8B restoring wetlands—benefits now valued up to $434B
item.description: China's coastal wetland restoration projects between 2000 and 2020 showed substantial economic gains. Investments of up to $13.8 billion generated ecosystem benefits valued as high as $434 billion. Mangrove restoration projects, in particular, offered exceptional benefit-cost ratios of 47 to 1. These restored wetlands provide vital carbon storage and coastal protection services. The research highlights restoration as a valuable nature-based solution for climate action.

item.title: Quote of the day by Joan of Arc: "All I have done is by Our Lord's command… I have done nothing in the world but…"
item.description: Joan of Arc attributed her extraordinary courage to divine command, not personal ambition. She faced her trial with humility, placing all credit with God. Her conviction provided strength through imprisonment and intense pressure. Purpose, rather than recognition, fueled her unwavering dedication to her mission. This historical figure's story continues to resonate due to her steadfast faith.

item.title: Scientists drilled 1,640 feet beneath Michigan and found 689 kinds of fungi living in water
item.description: A fascinating discovery in Michigan reveals 689 fungal species living in ancient groundwater that hasn't touched the surface since the last Ice Age 11,000 years ago. This unique ecosystem, concealed within deep rocks and water, also harbors tiny organisms like worms and tardigrades. Such findings could revolutionize our understanding of subsurface life and fundamentally alter how scientists track the movement of underground carbon.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Tourist feeding helped push Japan’s famous Rabbit Island beyond its natural limits
item.description: The unchecked practice of tourists feeding rabbits on Okunoshima has led to an overwhelming rise in their population, creating serious ecological concerns. This steady food source is altering animal behaviors, with wild boars starting to hunt rabbits more frequently. The plant life suffers, evident in the stark 'rabbit line' marking the landscape. Experts suggest implementing regulated feeding practices and formulating long-term conservation strategies for the island.
